subject.title: feat(ui): approval UX overhaul — inline cards, fair queue, shortcuts, badges

question: Should approval cards become the default active-session surface only when the chat pane is visibly reachable, with the modal retained as the fallback for hidden chat layouts?
rationale: This is a broad, security-adjacent interaction redesign; the mechanical fallback fix is clear, but maintainers need to confirm the intended permanent presentation contract for dashboards and responsive layouts.

options.title: Require visible-surface fallback
options.body: Keep inline cards for visible active chats, but retain the modal whenever the card cannot be reached; add focused dashboard/mobile coverage and live proof.

options.title: Keep modal authority
options.body: Show inline cards as a duplicate convenience surface while always retaining the approval in the modal queue.

options.title: Pause the redesign
options.body: Keep the existing modal-only behavior until maintainers choose a smaller approval UX scope.

recommendation.title: Require visible-surface fallback
recommendation.body: Keep inline cards for visible active chats, but retain the modal whenever the card cannot be reached; add focused dashboard/mobile coverage and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor is the current recent area contributor for the approval UX branch and has public OpenClaw history adjacent to exec-approval work.
